title: Fallowridge Activation Immersion Kickoff

SE to run initial perf smoke test and share spreadsheet

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09 14:30 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moran, Jordan Lee, Priya Patel (Redwood); Maya Ortiz, Samir Khan, Leah Brooks, Ethan Price (Fallowridge)
Shared artifacts: kickoff deck (https://redwood.app/s/ff/fallowridge-kickoff), pilot-runbook template (link in notes)

00:00 Alex Moran: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick roundtable, i'm alex from Redwood, i'm your AE. Priya CSM and Jordan our SE are here. how's everyone doing?
00:12 Maya Ortiz: good thanks, morning here. excited to get going. i'll be owning platform side.
00:20 Priya Patel: yes hi, we'll keep this practical — want to walk runway and what a successful pilot looks like.
00:30 Jordan Lee: i will go over runtime expectations and initial perf gating, and then we can dive into network and security.

02:05 Jordan Lee: quick note on what we typically see — for a pilot most customers start on hosted API to iterate then move to dedicated or private for noise and isolation. that's not prescriptive just typical.
02:20 Samir Khan: can we talk about VPC peering and egress rules? we have very tight network controls and only allow a few CIDR ranges out, also proxies.
02:34 Jordan Lee: absolutely, we support VPC peering and private deployments. for hosted we do a secure peering via a managed tunnel, for Private you'll want direct peering. do you have a preferred cloud?
02:47 Maya Ortiz: we're on AWS us-west-2, and we prefer peering to avoid egress costs.
03:03 Jordan Lee: cool — we'll need the staging VPC CIDR and the infra contact so we can set the peering up, and we'll coordinate the security handshakes.

05:30 Leah Brooks: from security perspective we need KMS integration for key management, SAML SSO for console access, and full audit logs retention details. are you SOC2 certified?
05:44 Alex Moran: yes we are SOC2 Type II, i'll share the report. quick callout sometimes the report is redacted for customer names but we can give the controls matrix.
05:56 Maya Ortiz: okay great, send that over. also we need to understand encryption at rest — do you do customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed?
06:08 Priya Patel: both options. for Private deployments we can wire customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we support BYOK with KMS — Jordan i'll let you add detail.
06:18 Jordan Lee: yeah, hosted supports customer KMS via cross-account key policies, there is a brief setup. for on-prem or VPC Private we can integrate with your KMS endpoint. note: sometimes docs say "Redwood Privet" in the auto-transcripts oops — we call it Redwood Private.

09:01 Ethan Price: what's the usual time to set up peering + KMS? just to plan timelines.
09:10 Jordan Lee: peas and peas — sorry, peering and KMS -- typically 3-5 business days for network + key setup if contacts are responsive. planning buffer is important.

11:00 Alex Moran: let's talk pilot scope. recommended start: ingest small set of customer prompts in staging, validate latency SLOs, validate cost per 1k tokens, and run some evals for quality drift. success criteria?
11:18 Maya Ortiz: our goals: avg p95 latency < 450ms for short prompts, throughput 30 qps sustained, and cost under our threshold. also no PII leakage on logs.
11:35 Priya Patel: noted. we'll define measurement plan. Jordan — can you suggest perf targets and the typical load profile?
11:44 Jordan Lee: sure, for our dedicated medium pool you should hit 30 qps with p95 ~300-500ms depending on context length. K-V cache and batching settings will impact cost — small prompts benefit from aggressive batching, long conversations change that.
11:58 Samir Khan: you mentioned K-V cash earlier? is that cash or cache in transcripts?
12:05 Jordan Lee: it's KV cache — the transcript often spells it K-V cash, but it's key-value cache for token cache between steps. helps reduce recompute for long chats.

15:22 Maya Ortiz: what's the instrumenting/observability story — we need logs for every token cost and tracing back to customer request ids.
15:30 Priya Patel: Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks. we can add a log forwarder to your SIEM; Jordan can walk through the API.
15:45 Jordan Lee: yes, we emit structured tracing metadata and request ids. one caveat: for hosted we redact some payloads by default but you can opt-in with DLP terms; for private you control retention.

19:02 Leah Brooks: audit logs retention and access control: we need RBAC, SSO integration, and exportable audit logs for 7 years per our retention policy. is 7 years supported?
19:16 Alex Moran: our standard retention window is 13 months on hosted logs; enterprise add-on supports longer retention and export to your S3. for 7 years we recommend private deployment or our long-retention add-on — i'll include options in the security package.
19:32 Leah Brooks: also want to confirm SOC2 attachments and PCI/ISO questions, but that's later.

22:40 Jordan Lee: on model pinning and rollouts — you can pin model versions per route, and our rollout engine supports canary, A/B and auto-fallback to a smaller model when capacity constrained. important for predictable latency.
22:57 Ethan Price: will the auto-fallback change output too much? our UX depends on consistent answers.
23:10 Jordan Lee: there can be quality differences; we recommend synthetic evals and a fallback policy that keeps output within a quality band. Redwood Optimize can propose quantization and batching tradeoffs.

26:00 Priya Patel: admin stuff: we'll produce an activation runbook template, request lists for firewall/CIDR, and an ops contact list. we'll also schedule a staging handoff session with Jordan in two weeks.
26:14 Maya Ortiz: good. can you also share the pilot metrics spreadsheet?
26:20 Jordan Lee: yes i'll upload a perf spreadsheet (link in deck) with columns for p50/p95 throughput, token count, model, batch settings.

30:10 Samir Khan: about cost controls — do you have quotas and rate-limiting we can enforce per route?
30:20 Alex Moran: yep, we support per-route quotas, rate limits, and token caps. you can combine that with autoscaling policies on Dedicated.
30:35 Samir Khan: fine. also need to test burst behavior — how the system degrades.
30:42 Jordan Lee: we have graceful degradation strategies: fallback model, circuit-breaker to queue requests, and priority routing. we'll script a scenario for the smoke test.

34:05 Maya Ortiz: final ask: what specifically do you need from us to get started?
34:12 Priya Patel: short list — staging VPC CIDR + infra point of contact, SAML metadata for SSO, KMS policy/account info if BYOK, sample prompt corpus (redacted), and sign-off on pilot dates.
34:28 Maya Ortiz: we'll get that by Friday.

38:00 Alex Moran: recap: Redwood sends security package + SOC2 + runbook by Thursday (2026-11-12), Jordan runs perf smoke and uploads results by 2026-11-18, customer provides VPC info by 2026-11-13, pilot kickoff target 2026-11-22. agreed?
38:20 Maya Ortiz: agreed.
38:30 Leah Brooks: also i'll send a list of compliance questions — can you route to security?
38:35 Alex Moran: yes, route to priya and security.

41:00 Jordan Lee: quick technical note: when you run the smoke we'll try a 10k token and 64 token contexts; please expect p95 to vary. also we might ask to tweak quantization to speed up.
41:18 Ethan Price: understood.

44:50 Alex Moran: thanks everyone — i'll capture the action items and drop calendar invites for the staging handoff and pilot kickoff. Priya will own runbook delivery.
44:59 Priya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
45:07 Maya Ortiz: thanks team, talk soon.

[End of transcript]
